title: A link needed to reach another screen. Several applications were involved.
intro: A Windows Phone app. A Chrome extension. A pairing flow. A web API. At the other end of all that: a new browser tab.
paragraphs: SendToChrome was a 2015 experiment in getting a URL from a Windows Phone to a desktop browser. The repository contains both clients and the web API between them. A short README manages to make the whole thing sound much smaller than it is.

The phone requested a pairing code. In the browser, a person entered that code and gave the browser instance a name. The system could then associate the device with its browsers and route a URL to a selected instance.
The Chrome extension listened for a Google Cloud Messaging event. When one arrived, it opened the URL in a new tab. A pleasantly ordinary result at the end of a rather elaborate journey.

That flow is visible in the implementation. Whether every part worked reliably in daily use is not established by the surviving code. This is a preserved mechanism, not a claim of a successful product. The original reason for building it is a story the code does not tell.
aside: The smallest result in the system was the thing it was built to move.
